## `reports/gadget_pkdgrav3_potential/run_stacks_local.sh`

Source: [run_stacks_local.sh](../../reports/gadget_pkdgrav3_potential/run_stacks_local.sh)

```text
The stacked-potential files of the report (data/<run>/profiles/), made on a workstation from copies of the four
outputs closest to z = 3, 1, 0.5, 0 (snapshots, pkdgrav3 p.par, halo catalogues):
  <kind>_out<i>.npz          particle-weighted, 36 log bins 0.02-50 Mpc/h        (gadget, pkd, pkc)
  <kind>_out<i>_lin.npz      particle-weighted, linear bins 0-50 Mpc/h, 0.2 wide  (gadget, pkd, pkc)
  <kind>_out<i>_vol.npz      volume-weighted (grid points), log bins             (gadget, pkd)
```

## `scripts/gadget_pkdgrav3_compare/job_compare.pbs`

Source: [job_compare.pbs](../../scripts/gadget_pkdgrav3_compare/job_compare.pbs)

```text
Potential comparison after both runs and their halo stages:
  1. compare_potential.py: particle by particle and matched halos, every output
  2. halo_potential_profile.py: stacked potential profiles (comoving Mpc/h, mass bins; stacks only) around halos
     at the outputs closest to PROF_Z, Gadget-4 and pkdgrav3 (HDF5 and .pkc), each with its own consistent-trees
     halos; pkdgrav3 without its self-term and aligned by offset_median of particles.csv (zero-point difference)
  3. compare_halos.py: mass functions, matched halos, VAHC quantities, at the outputs of particles.csv
qsub -v CONF=<compare32.conf>,PIPE_ENV=<repo>/scripts/pkdgrav3_pipeline/pipeline_env.sh,STAGE=compare
```

## `scripts/gadget_pkdgrav3_compare/job_gadget.pbs`

Source: [job_gadget.pbs](../../scripts/gadget_pkdgrav3_compare/job_gadget.pbs)

```text
Gadget-4 run of the comparison, the Sahyadri way (scripts/submit_CiPod.sh + scripts/gadget/run_gadget.sh):
  1. CLASS P(k) at Z_START (config/transfer/class_template_As.ini, scripts/assist/modify_class_output.py)
  2. NGenIC (2LPT) ICs, RestartFlag 6 -> $GADGET_DIR/ics/snapshot_ics_000.hdf5
  3. the same ICs for pkdgrav3 -> $IC_FILE (gadget4_ic_to_gadget2.py)
  4. Gadget-4 from the IC file -> $GADGET_DIR/snapshot_<nnn>.hdf5 (with Potential)
  5. snapnames.txt (for Rockstar) and gadget_out_z.txt (redshifts of the snapshots, pkdgrav3's dRedTo)
qsub -v CONF=<compare32_gadget.conf>,PIPE_ENV=<repo>/scripts/pkdgrav3_pipeline/pipeline_env.sh,STAGE=gadget
```

## `scripts/gadget_pkdgrav3_compare/setup_gadget4_pawna.sh`

Source: [setup_gadget4_pawna.sh](../../scripts/gadget_pkdgrav3_compare/setup_gadget4_pawna.sh)

```text
Build the two Gadget-4 executables of the Sahyadri workflow for one particle number, in the directory layout that
scripts/gadget/run_gadget.sh expects:
  <G4HOME>/code/Gadget-4/mesh<2N>-NGenIC/Gadget4   creates the ICs (RestartFlag 6)
  <G4HOME>/code/Gadget-4/mesh<2N>/Gadget4          runs from the IC file
(run_gadget.sh names the directory after NMESH = 2 * NPART = PMGRID.)

The source is copied to <G4HOME>/code/Gadget-4/gadget4 first, so nothing is written into it.

"pawna" as in the existing Sahyadri builds.
```

## `scripts/gadget_pkdgrav3_compare/submit_compare.sh`

Source: [submit_compare.sh](../../scripts/gadget_pkdgrav3_compare/submit_compare.sh)

```text
Submit the whole Gadget-4 vs pkdgrav3 comparison as a chain of PBS jobs:
  gadget (CLASS, NGenIC ICs, IC conversion, Gadget-4 run)
    -> pkdgrav3 from the same ICs: sim -> rockstar -> ctrees [-> vahc]   (pkdgrav3_pipeline, <name>.conf)
    -> Gadget-4 halos:             rockstar -> ctrees [-> vahc]          (pkdgrav3_pipeline, <name>_gadget.conf)
  -> compare (after the last stage of both)
  stages: CMP_PKD_STAGES / CMP_G4_STAGES in the config (default sim,rockstar,ctrees / rockstar,ctrees)
usage: submit_compare.sh <compare32.conf|compare256.conf> [--dry-run] [--hold]
  the Gadget-4 config is <dir of conf>/<name>_gadget.conf
```

## `scripts/pkdgrav3_pipeline/build_pkdgrav3_gpu_pegasus.sh`

Source: [build_pkdgrav3_gpu_pegasus.sh](../../scripts/pkdgrav3_pipeline/build_pkdgrav3_gpu_pegasus.sh)

```text
GPU (CUDA) build of pkdgrav3 for the pegasus GPU nodes (gpu001-004: one Tesla P100 16 GB each, compute capability 6.0,
driver 525.60.13 = CUDA 12.0). A separate build next to the CPU build: $PKD_IO_ROOT/build_gpu/pkdgrav3 (the CPU build
$PKD_IO_ROOT/build is not touched). Simulations use it with SIM_GPU=1 in run.conf (setup_production.py --sim-gpu;
planned_runs.txt option gpu=1).

  bash build_pkdgrav3_gpu_pegasus.sh            # on the pegasus login node (needs the internet for conda)
  PKD_IO_ROOT=... NJ=8 bash build_pkdgrav3_gpu_pegasus.sh

Compilers: CUDA 12.0's nvcc accepts host gcc <= 12, and gcc 12's headers (amxtileintrin.h, avx512fp16intrin.h) do
not compile under nvcc 12.0, so gcc 11. The WHOLE build must use the same gcc 11: a build with the CPU environment's
gcc 15 for C++ and gcc 11 only for the CUDA host code crashes at the first GPU work package
(mdl::CUDA::launch / mdl::gpu::Client::flushCompleted, SIGSEGV). MPI, HDF5, FFTW, GSL and Python come from the CPU
build's conda environment ($PKD_IO_ROOT/env, tools/pegasus/env_pegasus.sh), so both builds run with the same
run-time environment. CUDA toolkit and gcc 11: conda environment $PKD_IO_ROOT/env_cuda (created here).

Measured (2026-11-16, 512^3 L200 restart at z = 0.06): one GPU node 10.3 s/step against 36.1 s on a CPU node (2 MPI
ranks x 16 threads both), 100 % of the gravity tiles on the GPU; 2 GPU nodes 5.7 s/step; snapshots agree with the
CPU build to better than two CPU runs with different thread counts (positions rms 0.010 kpc/h, P(k) < 2e-7).
amgr charges a GPU like one more core (a GPU node-hour = 33 units).
```

## `scripts/pkdgrav3_pipeline/install_corrfunc.sh`

Source: [install_corrfunc.sh](../../scripts/pkdgrav3_pipeline/install_corrfunc.sh)

```text
Install Corrfunc from Arnaud de Mattia's fork (github.com/adematti/Corrfunc, branch desi: signed mu, i.e. the odd
multipoles) into a Python environment, for scripts/post-process/halo_xi_multipoles.py (stage ximult).

usage: install_corrfunc.sh <python> [workdir]
  python   the venv's python (e.g. $CODES/venv/bin/python); numpy must be installed in it
  workdir  where the source is cloned (default: a temporary directory, removed afterwards)
Environment: CORRFUNC_REPO (default https://github.com/adematti/Corrfunc), CORRFUNC_REF (default desi),
             LIBOMP_PREFIX (Mac; default $(brew --prefix libomp) or /opt/homebrew/opt/libomp)

Two patches of Corrfunc's common.mk, applied only where they are needed:
 - Linux: numpy's include directory first. Corrfunc puts -isystem <python include> before numpy's, and on
   Debian/Ubuntu with the python3-numpy package <python include>/numpy is the *system* numpy (1.x) headers, so a
   venv with numpy 2 got an extension that fails with "numpy.core.multiarray failed to import" (pawna, 2026-11-12).
 - Mac: Apple clang has no OpenMP and Homebrew gcc rejects Corrfunc's -march=apple-m1, so OpenMP comes from
   Homebrew's libomp (brew install libomp) with clang; without it the build is serial (about 7x slower on 8 cores).
The build uses this python's numpy (--no-build-isolation; needs setuptools and wheel, installed here).
Finally a smoke test: signed mu bins from -1 to 1, and whether the extension is linked to OpenMP.
```

## `scripts/pkdgrav3_pipeline/install_production.sh`

Source: [install_production.sh](../../scripts/pkdgrav3_pipeline/install_production.sh)

```text
Production install of everything the Sahyadri pipeline needs on one site, in a new directory:
  <root>/pkdgrav3_io        pkdgrav3 (GitHub main) + snapcomp tools; pawna: own venv for pkdgrav3's embedded
                            Python (dill, tomli, Cython); pegasus, swarm: conda env (MPI, HDF5, FFTW)
  <root>/sahyadri-sandbox   this repository (branch run-manager): pipeline, post-processing, run manager
  <root>/codes              Rockstar (.pkc reader), consistent-trees, Python venv (requirements.txt), C helpers

usage: install_production.sh pawna   [/user/$USER/sahyadri_prod]
       install_production.sh pegasus [~/sahyadri_pipeline]
       install_production.sh swarm   [/user1/$USER/sahyadri_pipeline]   (Miniforge in /user1/$USER/miniforge3 if
                                      missing; pkdgrav3 for Ice Lake; no 'bash -l': swarm's login shell drops the
                                      arguments of a script started that way)
Rerunning updates the clones and rebuilds. Nothing outside <root> is changed (pegasus: caches on /data).
```

## `scripts/pkdgrav3_pipeline/job_archive.pbs`

Source: [job_archive.pbs](../../scripts/pkdgrav3_pipeline/job_archive.pbs)

```text
Stage archive (after verify): the kept files (retention.py) copied SCRATCH -> ARCHIVE, read back from the disk
and compared (SHA-256), MANIFEST.json + SHA256SUMS written, the archive made read-only (archive_run.py).
Nothing in SCRATCH is deleted (that is done by the manager after approval). Restart: rerun (checked files skipped).
ARCHIVE_UPTO=N (stage archb, started by the manager while the simulation runs): only the kept particle files of
snapshots 0..N (archive_run.py --particles-upto N); no manifest, nothing locked; event archive_batch_done.
The manager runs this script as a process on its own (head) node, not through PBS (archive_on_head).
```

## `scripts/pkdgrav3_pipeline/job_ctrees.pbs`

Source: [job_ctrees.pbs](../../scripts/pkdgrav3_pipeline/job_ctrees.pbs)

```text
Stage 3: consistent-trees (Sahyadri-patched: w0-wa and curvature) on the Rockstar outputs, then
clean_trees.pl as in the pegasus pipeline: hlists -> $HALO_DIR/out_<snap>.trees, scales.txt -> ../scales.txt,
configs kept in logs/, Rockstar's out_*.list / halos_* / hlists / outputs deleted (CLEAN_ROCKSTAR=0 keeps them
and only copies the hlists).
Restart: rerun; consistent-trees starts over from the Rockstar outputs (needs CLEAN_ROCKSTAR=0 on the earlier run
if it had already cleaned).
```

## `scripts/pkdgrav3_pipeline/job_fits.pbs`

Source: [job_fits.pbs](../../scripts/pkdgrav3_pipeline/job_fits.pbs)

```text
Stage 5: ASCII halo catalogs and trees -> FITS (.fits.gz) with metadata, then an independent check.
  $HALO_DIR/out_<snap>.trees/.vahc/.tens -> $HALO_DIR/compressed/out_<snap>_{basic,extended,vahc,tens}.fits.gz
  $HALO_DIR/trees/tree_*.dat, locations.dat, forests.list -> $HALO_DIR/compressed/trees/
FITS_DELETE_ASCII=1 deletes each ASCII file after its FITS file was written and verified.
Restart: rerun; existing FITS files are skipped.
```

## `scripts/pkdgrav3_pipeline/job_parquet.pbs`

Source: [job_parquet.pbs](../../scripts/pkdgrav3_pipeline/job_parquet.pbs)

```text
Stage parquet (after fits): a Parquet copy of every FITS table and tree file, in a parallel directory with the same
names (fits_to_parquet.py: streamed in row blocks, low memory; each file checked against the FITS DATASUM and
read back with per-column hashes):
  $HALO_DIR/compressed/out_<snap>_<table>.fits.gz -> $HALO_DIR/parquet/out_<snap>_<table>.parquet
  $HALO_DIR/compressed/trees/*.fits.gz            -> $HALO_DIR/parquet/trees/*.parquet
Archived with the FITS (retention.py) and checked in stage verify. PARQUET=0 in run.conf: nothing to do.
Restart: rerun; files already converted from the current FITS (size and mtime recorded in the Parquet) are skipped.
```

## `scripts/pkdgrav3_pipeline/job_rockstar.pbs`

Source: [job_rockstar.pbs](../../scripts/pkdgrav3_pipeline/job_rockstar.pbs)

```text
Stage 2: Rockstar on all outputs, reading the .pkc snapshots directly (FILE_FORMAT = "PKC"), or Gadget-4 HDF5
snapshots snapshot_<snap>.hdf5 in $SIM_DIR when the config sets SIM_CODE=gadget4 (FILE_FORMAT = "AREPO").
Server and client run in this one job on one node. Output: $HALO_DIR/out_<snap>.list, rockstar.cfg (the full
configuration Rockstar used), restart.cfg and the newest snapshot's halos_<snap>.*.bin (for restarts).
RS_LOCAL_OUT=1 (default): Rockstar writes to the node's local disk (RS_LOCAL_DIR, default /var/tmp), and the
  finished out_<snap>.list, restart.cfg and the newest halos_<snap>.*.bin are copied to $HALO_DIR every
  RS_SYNC_S seconds and at the end. Rockstar writes its halo files inside the halo-finding phase, so on /storage
  (NFS) that phase waits for the disk: 188 s -> 114 s for two 512^3 snapshots (pawna job 2536781).
  RS_LOCAL_OUT=0: write to $HALO_DIR directly (as before; all halos_<snap>.* kept).
Writers: one per core of the job (PBS_NCPUS, NCPUS, else RS_NCPU) unless RS_WRITERS_FIXED=1 (then the configuration's NUM_WRITERS):
  16 -> 32 -> 64 writers took 114 -> 78 -> 64 s in the same test, peak memory 7.5 -> 7.4 -> 8.1 GB.
Restart: rerun the job; it starts from scratch unless RS_RESTART=1 (then Rockstar's restart.cfg is used).
Batches (RS_SNAP_FIRST=<a> RS_SNAP_LAST=<b>, set by tools/sahyadri_manager while the simulation runs): snapshots
  a..b only, with the snapshot list cut after b (the planned outputs of output_steps.txt, so the simulation need not
  have finished) and RESTART_SNAP = a: Rockstar reads the halos_<a-1>.*.bin of the previous batch (kept in
  $HALO_DIR) for the merger links. Same catalogues as one run over all snapshots (pawna test, t128/batch vs single).
```

## `scripts/pkdgrav3_pipeline/job_sim.pbs`

Source: [job_sim.pbs](../../scripts/pkdgrav3_pipeline/job_sim.pbs)

```text
Stage 1: pkdgrav3 simulation -> $PKC_DIR/snap.<step>.s<pct>.<writer>.pkc (+ $SIM_DIR/snapnames.txt for Rockstar).
Submit with submit_pipeline.sh (or: qsub -v CONF=<run.conf>,PIPE_ENV=<this dir>/pipeline_env.sh -l select=1:ncpus=192:mem=700gb job_sim.pbs).
Parameter file: $PKD_PAR if the config sets it (written by setup_production.py), else p.par generated from the
config by make_pkdgrav3_par.py.
Restart: RESTART=<checkpoint> (or RESTART=latest: newest checkpoints/*.chk) continues from a checkpoint
(submit_pipeline.sh --restart latest). Without RESTART the simulation starts again from the ICs.
Outputs: if $SIM_DIR/output_steps.txt exists (planned output steps), snapnames.txt lists exactly those steps
(a snapshot written when pkdgrav3 stops at iWallRunTime or on a STOP file is not a planned output and is ignored).
SIM_STAGING=1: snapshots and checkpoints staged on the node's local SSD and drained to NFS during the run.
```

## `scripts/pkdgrav3_pipeline/job_vahc.pbs`

Source: [job_vahc.pbs](../../scripts/pkdgrav3_pipeline/job_vahc.pbs)

```text
Stage 4: value-added catalogs out_<snap>.vahc (and .tens with PP_TENS=1) from the .pkc particles and the
consistent-trees catalogs out_<snap>.trees (post-process/run_addvalue.py; production settings).
Restart: rerun; snapshots whose outputs exist are skipped.
```

## `scripts/pkdgrav3_pipeline/job_verify.pbs`

Source: [job_verify.pbs](../../scripts/pkdgrav3_pipeline/job_verify.pbs)

```text
Stage verify (after fits): everything computed and consistent (verify_run.py) -> $STATE_DIR/verify.json.
Reads every snapshot's .pkc headers and trailers, the halo catalogues' IDs (binary) and FITS row counts, and runs pkc_check (every
particle ID once) on the kept full snapshots, several at once. Restart: rerun (pkc_check passes are cached).
```

## `scripts/pkdgrav3_pipeline/job_vpot.pbs`

Source: [job_vpot.pbs](../../scripts/pkdgrav3_pipeline/job_vpot.pbs)

```text
Post-processing stage vpot (not run by the manager; postprocess.sh vpot): halo potential profiles out_<snap>.vpot
(mean particle potential within rs, R200b and at the .vahc scales; vahc_fast.py) for the outputs whose .pkc store
the potential (z <= 0.5 in production). Only .vpot is computed (--no-vahc); existing .vpot are skipped.
Run stage fits after it: the vahc FITS tables of those outputs are rewritten with the phi_* columns (HAS_VPOT).
```

## `scripts/pkdgrav3_pipeline/job_vprof.pbs`

Source: [job_vprof.pbs](../../scripts/pkdgrav3_pipeline/job_vprof.pbs)

```text
Optional stage after the halo catalogues: stacked potential profiles around halos (volume weighted by default),
scripts/gadget_pkdgrav3_compare/halo_potential_profile.py on the .pkc snapshots that store the potential and the
consistent-trees catalogues out_<snap>.trees. Mean, scatter and jackknife error of phi in shells of comoving r
around host halos, per mass bin (the same bins as stage xcorr). Volume weighting: the code's potential is put on a
grid (local linear fit to the k nearest particles) and the grid points are stacked, so every shell is an average
over space, not over mass.
  submit_pipeline.sh <run.conf> --stages vprof         (postprocess.sh vprof; manager page: post-processing)
Config (all optional):
  VPROF_SNAPS    snapshots, comma separated; default (or "all"): every output whose .pkc store the potential
                 (z <= 0.5 in production); "last": the last one only
  VPROF_WEIGHT   volume | particle | "volume particle" (default volume)
  VPROF_MBINS    halo mass bin edges, Msun/h, Mvir (default: --mbins of XC_ARGS, else the xcorr default
                 2e12,1e13,5e13,2e14,1e16)
  VPROF_RBINS    radial bins (default 0.02,50,36: 36 log bins 0.02-50 Mpc/h; lin:0,50,0.2 for linear)
  VPROF_SUB      .pkc subsamples read (default: all particles); e.g. 1,3,5 (9 %) for 2048^3, where all particles
                 in one KD-tree for the gridding do not fit in memory
  VPROF_ARGS     other options of halo_potential_profile.py (default: --max-halos 20000 per bin, --target 8192
                 for volume weighting, grid 2 x the particle grid per side)
  VPROF_NCPU, VPROF_MEM, VPROF_WALL   resources (default 32 cores, 160gb, 48 h; used by submit_pipeline.sh)
                 Measured (pawna, 32 cores, /usr/bin/time -v): 512^3, grid 1024^3: 7.9 min per snapshot, 15 GB max
                 RSS of one process; 37 snapshots ~5 h. The grid fit scales with grid points (~8x for 1024^3 particles).
Output: $HALO_DIR/vprof/out_<snap>_vprof_<weight>.npz (kept with the run). Restart: rerun; existing outputs are
skipped. The gridded potential (4 bytes per grid point) is a temporary file in $HALO_DIR/vprof/tmp, removed after
each snapshot.
```

## `scripts/pkdgrav3_pipeline/job_xcorr.pbs`

Source: [job_xcorr.pbs](../../scripts/pkdgrav3_pipeline/job_xcorr.pbs)

```text
Optional stage after fits: halo-halo potential cross-correlation (scripts/post-process/halo_potential_xcorr.py)
from $HALO_DIR/compressed/out_<snap>_{basic,vahc}.fits.gz (the vahc file needs the .vpot columns: PP_POT=1).
  submit_pipeline.sh <run.conf> --stages xcorr          (or --stages vahc,fits,xcorr)
Config (all optional):
  XC_SNAPS   snapshots, comma separated; default (or "all"): every snapshot with out_<snap>.vpot, i.e. every output
             that stores the potential (z <= 0.5 in production); "last": the last one only
  XC_ARGS    options of halo_potential_xcorr.py (default: its defaults, log:0.2,50,30 bins, profile mass bins,
             phi_Rvir,phi_rs,phi_R1p5vir,phi_R0p5vir,phi_R200b); e.g. XC_ARGS="--rbins lin:0,50,0.2"
  XC_TAG     output name tag (default: log or lin from --rbins)
  XC_NCPU, XC_MEM, XC_WALL   resources (default 16 cores, 16gb, 24 h; used by submit_pipeline.sh)
Output: $HALO_DIR/xcorr/out_<snap>_xcorr_<tag>.npz. Restart: rerun; existing outputs are skipped.
```

## `scripts/pkdgrav3_pipeline/job_ximult.pbs`

Source: [job_ximult.pbs](../../scripts/pkdgrav3_pipeline/job_ximult.pbs)

```text
Optional stage after fits: halo-halo correlation multipoles (l = 0..4, dipole included) between mass bins in real
space, redshift space and with the gravitational-redshift shift of the halo potential
(scripts/post-process/halo_xi_multipoles.py; needs the Corrfunc fork with signed mu in the venv:
install_corrfunc.sh, guide section 14).
  submit_pipeline.sh <run.conf> --stages ximult          (or --stages vahc,fits,ximult)
Config (all optional):
  XM_SNAPS   snapshots, comma separated (default: the last one, z = 0)
  XM_ARGS    options of halo_xi_multipoles.py (default: its defaults: real,rsd,grav,rsd+grav; phi_rs; los z;
             lin:0,100,2; 200 mu bins; l = 0..4), e.g. XM_ARGS="--los x,y,z"
  XM_TAG     output name tag (default: ximult)
  XM_NCPU, XM_MEM, XM_WALL   resources (default 32 cores, 32gb, 6 h; used by submit_pipeline.sh)
Output: $HALO_DIR/xcorr/out_<snap>_<tag>.npz. Restart: rerun; existing outputs are skipped.
```

## `scripts/pkdgrav3_pipeline/memmon.sh`

Source: [memmon.sh](../../scripts/pkdgrav3_pipeline/memmon.sh)

```text
Memory monitor: samples a process and all its descendants until the process exits (Linux /proc).
usage: memmon.sh <root pid> <out.tsv> [interval s, default 5] [pid to exclude with its descendants]
Each sample: sum over the processes of PSS (proportional set size: a shared page counts 1/n in each of
the n processes that map it, so the sum is the memory the job really occupies) and of RSS (shared pages
counted in every process: an upper bound, e.g. for Rockstar's forked readers).
Output lines "t_s nproc pss_kb rss_kb"; peaks shorter than the interval can be missed.
pawna puts all PBS jobs in one cgroup (/system.slice/pbs.service), so there is no per-job memory.peak.
```

## `scripts/pkdgrav3_pipeline/setup_pawna.sh`

Source: [setup_pawna.sh](../../scripts/pkdgrav3_pipeline/setup_pawna.sh)

```text
One-time setup of the halo codes and Python environment of the Sahyadri pkdgrav3 pipeline on pawna.

usage: setup_pawna.sh <CODES dir> [PKD_IO_ROOT]
  CODES        where to build (e.g. /storage/$USER/sahyadri_codes); the run configs point to it
  PKD_IO_ROOT  pkdgrav3 install (default /storage/$USER/pkdgrav3_io; set it up first with pkdgrav3's
               tools/pawna/setup_pawna.sh, see pkdgrav3 docs/running_on_pawna.md). Its snapcomp build
               provides the zstd library that Rockstar's .pkc reader links against.
Builds:
  $CODES/rockstar   Rockstar from github.com/shadaba/rockstar, branch sahyadri at ROCKSTAR_REF (upstream 36ce9eea36ee +
                    Sahyadri changes: PKC reader, curvature, w0-wa; see SAHYADRI.md there), make with_hdf5_pkc.
                    (public). If it cannot be fetched (no network to GitHub), the same source is made from
                    upstream 36ce9ee plus the older overlay kept here in code/Rockstar/.
  $CODES/ctrees     consistent-trees 7c20add + Sahyadri changes (w0-wa/curvature background), make
  $CODES/venv       Python 3 venv (own packages) + numpy scipy pandas h5py fitsio zstandard matplotlib classy, Corrfunc (fork)
  $CODES/lib        cic_update.so, ngp_update.so, vpot_sums.so, halo_pair_sums.so for post-process (SAHYADRI_LIBDIR)
Rerunning rebuilds everything (the clones are kept).
```

## `scripts/pkdgrav3_pipeline/submit_pipeline.sh`

Source: [submit_pipeline.sh](../../scripts/pkdgrav3_pipeline/submit_pipeline.sh)

```text
Submit the Sahyadri pkdgrav3 pipeline for one run as a chain of PBS jobs:
  sim -> rockstar -> ctrees -> vahc -> fits -> parquet   (each starts only if the previous one succeeded: afterok;
  parquet only with PARQUET=1 in run.conf: Parquet copy of the FITS in <halo dir>/parquet, job_parquet.pbs)
  optional, only when named in --stages: vpot (halo potential profiles, job_vpot.pbs; then fits again),
  xcorr (halo-halo potential cross-correlation, job_xcorr.pbs), vprof (stacked volume-weighted potential profiles
  around halos, job_vprof.pbs), ximult (halo correlation multipoles in real/redshift space with
  the gravitational-redshift shift, job_ximult.pbs); production runs: postprocess.sh in the run directory
  -> verify -> archive (checks; copy of the kept data to ARCHIVE, read-only), only when named in --stages
  (tools/sahyadri_manager submits them itself)
Rockstar batch: --stages rockstar --rs-snaps A-B (snapshots A..B, see job_rockstar.pbs)

usage: submit_pipeline.sh <run.conf> [--stages sim,rockstar,ctrees,vahc,fits,parquet] [--after JOBID] [--hold] [--restart CHK] [--dry-run]
  --stages  any subset, in pipeline order (e.g. "ctrees,vahc,fits" to redo the later stages)
  --after   make the first stage wait for an existing job (afterok), e.g. a running simulation
  --hold    submit the first job held (qrls <id> to start the chain)
  --restart CHK  the sim stage continues from checkpoint CHK (latest = newest $SIM_DIR/checkpoints/*.chk)
  --dry-run print the qsub commands only
Prints the job ids; the chain is also written to $LOGS/chain.<run>.<date>.txt.
```

## `scripts/pkdgrav3_pipeline/swarm/env_swarm.sh`

Source: [env_swarm.sh](../../scripts/pkdgrav3_pipeline/swarm/env_swarm.sh)

```text
pkdgrav3 run-time environment on swarm (TIFR; 12 nodes x 64 Ice Lake cores, 504 GB; 10 Gb/s Ethernet with RoCE).
Sourced by job_sim.pbs (SIM_ENV in run.conf). The conda environment and its Open MPI 5 (UCX) are those of pkdgrav3's
pegasus set-up (tools/pegasus/env_pegasus.sh); swarm adds:
  - mpirun starts its daemons on the other nodes with ssh; with the conda library path the system ssh loads conda's
    OpenSSL and fails ("OpenSSL version mismatch"): ssh_noconda (next to this file) runs it without that path
  - CONDA_BASE: Miniforge in /user1 (install_production.sh swarm)
```

```text
PBS array job of the Gadget-4 chain: splits snapshots SNAP_START..N_OUT-1 into NJOBS_PP ranges and runs
postprocess.py on range $PBS_ARRAY_INDEX with NCPU_PP processes (particles down-sampled to 512^3 above 512^3).
  run_postprocess.sh <PYTHON_EXEC> <SIM_STEM> <REAL> <NPART> <SNAP_START> <N_OUT> <PP_GRID> <LBOX> <NJOBS_PP> <NCPU_PP>
```

## `scripts/rockstar/pkc_validation/rockstar_val.pbs`

Source: [rockstar_val.pbs](../../scripts/rockstar/pkc_validation/rockstar_val.pbs)

```text
Rockstar PKC reader validation on the 512^3 run (sahyadri-sandbox docs/rockstar_pkc_reader_plan.md, section 6).
Routes, all with NUM_BLOCKS = 8 over the 6 outputs:
  pkc   native PKC reader (run twice: pkc, pkc2 -> Rockstar's own run-to-run scatter)
  gad   pkc_to_gadget --blocks 8              (same particles as pkc, Gadget reader)
  h5g   pkc_to_gadget --blocks 8 --from-hdf5  (unquantized HDF5 particles, Gadget reader)
  pkcsub native PKC reader on the 1% + 3% subsamples only (PKC_SUBSAMPLES = "1,3", quick-look option)
Memory of every step (PSS/RSS of its process tree, scripts/pkdgrav3_pipeline/memmon.sh): $OUT/mem.<step>.tsv,
peaks in the log ("MEM <step>: ..."). Output directory: $OUT (qsub -v RSVAL_OUT=<name>, default rsval).
Exact test at the last output: fixed-seed test build, NUM_BLOCKS = NUM_WRITERS = 1: pkc1 vs gad1 byte-identical.
Then consistent-trees (Sahyadri-patched) on pkc and h5g. Gadget files live on the node's local disk only.
```

## `scripts/submit_CiPod.sh`

Source: [submit_CiPod.sh](../../scripts/submit_CiPod.sh)

```text
Submit the Gadget-4 chain of one run as dependent PBS jobs from a submission config file: CLASS transfer
function (prep_transfer.sh), Gadget-4 with NGenIC ICs (run_gadget.sh), Rockstar and consistent-trees,
post-processing (run_postprocess.sh) and the janitor. Paths (SANDBOX_DIR, CONFIG_DIR, SCRATCH_DIR) and switches
(RUN_CLASS, Rockstar, post-processing) are read from the config file. The pkdgrav3 pipeline replaces this on
pawna: scripts/pkdgrav3_pipeline/submit_pipeline.sh.
  submit_CiPod.sh <SUB_CONFIG_FILE>
```
